## Why the Right Food Container Matters

Poor food organization is a leading cause of food waste in Indonesian households. Data from Bappenas shows that approximately 23-48 million tons of food are wasted annually in Indonesia. Most of this is due to improper storage. For additional information, also see the guide from [The Spruce](https://www.thespruce.com/).
Quality food containers help:
- **Extend storage life** of food in the refrigerator and freezer
- **Prevent spills** and odors spreading inside the fridge
- **Simplify meal prep** for families or food businesses
- **Reduce food waste** because food doesn't spoil quickly
## Types of Food Containers by Material
### 1. Glass Food Containers (Borosilicate Glass)

Borosilicate glass is the premium choice for food containers. It withstands extreme temperatures (from -20 to 400 degrees Celsius), doesn't absorb odors, and is safe for microwaves and ovens. The downside is the heavier weight and risk of breaking. For additional information, also see the guide from [Real Simple](https://www.realsimple.com/).
### 2. BPA-Free Plastic Food Containers

Food-grade plastic that's BPA-free is the most popular choice because it's lightweight and affordable. Make sure to look for the "BPA-Free" label and a triangle symbol with the number 5 (PP - Polypropylene) which is safe for food.
### 3. Stainless Steel Food Containers
Stainless steel is extremely durable and doesn't react with acidic foods. Perfect for carrying lunch boxes and storing dry foods. Cannot be used in the microwave.
### 4. Silicone Food Containers
Silicone material is flexible and can be folded when not in use. Great for traveling and saving storage space.

## How to Care for Food Containers to Make Them Last
Proper care can extend the life of your food containers to 5-10 years. Here are care tips:
- **Hand wash** is more recommended than dishwasher to preserve the rubber seal
- **Don't use rough sponges** on plastic containers as they can scratch the surface and harbor bacteria
- **Dry completely** before storing to prevent mold and odors
- **Store without lids** when not in use for good air circulation
- **Replace rubber seals** every 1-2 years if they start hardening or no longer seal properly
## How to Choose the Right Food Container
### For Meal Prep

Choose a set of food containers with uniform sizes so they stack easily in your fridge. Glass material is more recommended because it can go straight into the microwave without needing to transfer to another container.
### For Food Business

If you sell food, choose [food containers for selling](/blog/wadah-makanan-untuk-jualan) that are food-grade, leak-proof, and look professional. Also consider disposable food containers made from eco-friendly materials.
### For Freezer Storage
Make sure the food container is labeled "freezer-safe". Not all plastics withstand freezing temperatures. Borosilicate glass and PP (Polypropylene) plastic are safe for freezer.

## Tips for Storing Food to Keep It Fresh Longer
![Tips for storing food with food containers to keep it fresher longer](/images/blog/food-container-tips.webp)
1. **Cool food first** before putting it in the container and fridge
2. **Don't fill completely** - leave 1-2 cm space for expansion in the freezer
3. **Label the date** on each container so you know the consumption order
4. **Separate wet and dry foods** to prevent excess moisture
5. **Clean immediately** after use to prevent stubborn stains
Good fridge organization starts with the right food container. Combine with other [essential kitchen equipment](/blog/peralatan-dapur-wajib-untuk-rumah-tangga-baru) for a more organized kitchen.

## Food Containers for Meal Prep: Practical Guide
Meal prep, or preparing meals for several days ahead, is becoming increasingly popular in Indonesia. Besides saving time, meal prep also helps control portions and food expenses.
### Meal Prep Steps with Food Containers
1. **Plan your menu** for 5-7 days ahead including breakfast, lunch, and dinner
2. **Shop for ingredients** all at once during the weekend for efficiency
3. **Batch cook** - prepare proteins, carbohydrates, and vegetables in large quantities
4. **Portion into containers** - divide according to your per-meal needs
5. **Label and arrange** in the fridge based on consumption order
### Best Food Containers for Meal Prep
For meal prep, choose food containers that are:
- **Microwave-safe** so you can heat directly without transferring to another container
- **Uniform size** (750ml-1L) so they stack easily in the fridge
- **Transparent** so you can see the contents without opening
- **Leak-proof** especially for foods with sauce
Good kitchen organization starts with the right storage containers. Also read [how to organize a small kitchen effectively](/blog/mengorganisir-dapur-kecil-dengan-efektif) for more tips.
## Dangers of Non-Safe Food Containers
Using food storage that isn't food-grade can have serious health impacts. Some risks to be aware of:
- **Chemical migration** - cheap plastic containers can release harmful substances like BPA and phthalates into food, especially when heated
- **Bacterial contamination** - non-airtight containers allow bacteria to multiply faster
- **Reaction with acidic foods** - aluminum or low-quality plastic containers can react with acidic foods like tomatoes and citrus
Always make sure your food container has food-grade certification and a BPA-free label. This isn't about prestige, it's about your family's safety.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
### Is plastic food container safe for hot food?
Only food containers made from PP (Polypropylene) with triangle symbol 5 are safe for hot food. Avoid plastics with symbols 3 (PVC) and 6 (PS/Styrofoam).
### How long can food be stored in a food container?
In the refrigerator (0-4 degrees C): rice 3-5 days, cooked vegetables 3-4 days, cooked meat 3-4 days. In the freezer (-18 degrees C): can last 1-3 months depending on the type of food.
### Which is better, glass or plastic food containers?

Glass is more hygienic, doesn't absorb odors, and lasts longer. Plastic is lighter and breakproof. For home use, glass is more recommended. For carrying when traveling, plastic or stainless steel is more practical.
### How do you remove odors from plastic food containers?
Soak in a baking soda solution (1 tablespoon per liter of water) for 30 minutes. Rinse thoroughly and dry in the sun. For stubborn stains, use a mixture of white vinegar and water.
### Can food containers be used in the microwave?
Make sure there's a "microwave-safe" label on the container. Always slightly open the lid when heating to prevent excessive pressure. Avoid heating stainless steel food containers in the microwave.
**Q: How long do quality home organization products typically last?**

With proper routine care, food-grade plastic products last 3-5 years, while borosilicate glass and grade 304 stainless steel can last 10+ years. Key factors are consistent maintenance and avoiding extreme temperature exposure.
**Q: Is this product food-safe?**

Ensure the product is labeled "food-grade" or "BPA-free" before using it for food storage. Safe materials include borosilicate glass, grade 304 stainless steel, and certified food-grade plastic. Avoid plastic without food safety certification, especially for hot or oily foods.
**Q: How do I clean and maintain it?**

Wash with mild dish soap and warm water. Avoid abrasive sponges that can scratch the surface. For stubborn stains, use a baking soda and water paste as a natural cleaner. Dry completely before storing to prevent mold and bacteria.
